patients with anti-Jo-1 antibodies display a distinct IgG Fc glycan profile, and that this profile is further enhanced in the anti-Jo-2 autoantibody fraction.
anti-Jo1 positive patients with idiopathic interstitial lung disease have a characteristic IgG-Fc-glycan signature that is further enriched in anti-Jo 1 autoantibody IgG.

the Fc-glycosylation profile of anti-Jo1 IgG differs significantly from healthy controls, and that this profile is further modified by the presence of anti-Jo-1 antibodies.
the anti-Jol+ patient Fc glycan profile is characteristic for this patient group and contains phenotype specific features, which may underlie pathogenicity of anti-Jo1.
the IgG Fc-Glycans of Jo1+ patients show characteristic features which are further enhanced in the anti-Jo-1 IgG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IgG1 FA2 Fc-glycosylation pattern is altered in ASS and Jo1+ patients.

anti-Jo1 patients have an IgG Fc glycosylation profile which is different from healthy controls and from patients with other autoimmune diseases, and this is further enhanced by enrichment of the anti-Jo autoantibodies.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the IgG Fc glycan profile is a useful tool to distinguish between Jo1+ patients from controls and to identify patients with ILD and ASS.
the Fc-glycoform composition of IgG1 in patients with anti-Jo-1 autoantibody is altered and that the Fc glycoforms of anti-Jo-antibodies are further altered.
